reason: The NEON transpose tests a distinct timed conversion for the correctly mapped TB call. The prior TB replay regressed, but whole-call scores do not isolate transpose cost, so this remains uncertain. Half-band packing and four-step unrolling test distinct changes, with risks from extra packing and register or scheduling pressure. TA adds a timed B transpose while retaining generated B packing and adding generated A packing, so its expected benefit is low. The 288-byte scratch stride has no cache evidence and increases scratch use; fused transpose repeats A-tile transpose work across 16 column panels. The four-tile K-pair proposal appears to alias the measured two-step unroll's load-then-compute schedule; it should be treated as an abstention, not a new experiment. None has established a speedup; retain the ten-report paired-control and held-out gates.
